fullPassage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were unwilling to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt — and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.

questions.passage: In 1900, electric systems had become a practical alternative. The technological advances ①<u>made</u> electric systems more affordable. The marketing programs also ②<u>sped</u> the adoption. Further ③<u>accelerated</u> the shift was the rapid expansion of skilled engineers. Electric power had gone from exotic to ④<u>commonplace</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 변화를 더 가속시킨(accelerating) 것은 확장이었다. ③ accelerated → accelerating: 현재분사가 와야 함.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ accelerated → accelerating: 'Further accelerating the shift was ~' 도치 구문. 현재분사(능동)가 필요.
✅ ① made: make+O+OC(형용사). 적절.
❌ ② sped: speed의 과거형. 적절.
❌ ④ commonplace: 형용사. 적절.
det.tip: Further + V-ing + O + was + S: 도치구문. 현재분사(능동) vs 과거분사(수동) 구별

questions.passage: Factories continued ①<u>to build</u> their own systems. Few manufacturers considered ②<u>to buy</u> electricity from central stations. ③<u>Designed</u> to supply lighting, the stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve big factories. Factory owners knew a glitch would bring operations to ④<u>a halt</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 구매하는 것을 고려했다(considered buying). ② to buy → buying: consider는 동명사를 목적어로 취함.
det.analysis:
❌ ② to buy → buying: consider + V-ing. to부정사는 불가.
✅ ① to build: continue + to V / V-ing 둘 다 가능. 적절.
❌ ③ Designed: 분사구문(= As they were designed). 적절.
❌ ④ a halt: bring to a halt 관용표현. 적절.
det.tip: consider + V-ing (동명사만 가능). cf. continue + to V / V-ing (둘 다 가능)

questions.passage: Less than 5 percent of the power ①<u>using</u> in factories came from electricity. The advances made systems affordable. Skilled engineers, ②<u>who</u> provided the expertise needed to install systems, expanded rapidly. Factory owners, ③<u>having</u> always supplied their own power, were unwilling to trust outsiders. A survey found 50,000 plants ④<u>in operation</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 공장에서 사용되는(used) 전력. ① using → used: power는 '사용되는' 것이므로 과거분사(수동)가 필요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① using → used: power와 use는 수동 관계. 'power used in factories' = 공장에서 사용된 전력.
✅ ② who: 관계대명사 주격. engineers를 선행사로 적절.
❌ ③ having: 완료 분사구문. 적절.
❌ ④ in operation: 전치사구. 적절.
det.tip: 현재분사(능동) vs 과거분사(수동): power used(사용된) / workers using(사용하는)

questions.passage: In the first decade ①<u>in which</u> electric systems became practical, advances made them affordable. The suppliers' intensive marketing ②<u>sped</u> adoption. Engineers provided expertise ③<u>to install</u> the systems. The factory owners knew that a lot of glitches might well ④<u>meant</u> bankruptcy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 많은 결함은 파산을 의미할(mean) 수 있었다. ④ meant → mean: might 뒤에 동사원형.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ meant → mean: 조동사 might 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 함.
✅ ① in which: 전치사+관계대명사. 적절.
❌ ② sped: speed의 과거형. 적절.
❌ ③ to install: expertise needed to install. to부정사 적절.
det.tip: 조동사(might/may/can/will) + 동사원형. might well = ~일 수도 있다

questions.passage: Electric systems had become a practical alternative. But technological advances made them more affordable. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid __________ in the number of skilled engineers who provided the expertise needed to install systems.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 숙련 엔지니어 수의 급격한 증가(expansion)가 변화를 가속시켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ expansion(확장/증가): 원문 일치.
❌ ① reduction(감소): 반의어.
❌ ② decline(감소): 반의어.
❌ ④ stagnation(정체): 증가의 반대.
det.tip: expansion(확장)↔reduction/decline(감소). rapid expansion = 급격한 증가

questions.passage: Factories continued to build their own systems. Central stations had neither the size nor the skill for big factories. Factory owners knew that a ①<u>glitch</u> in power supply would bring operations to a halt — and that glitches might mean ②<u>prosperity</u>. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion of skilled engineers. The factory owners were unwilling to assign a critical function to ③<u>an outsider</u>, preferring to maintain their own ④<u>premises</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 많은 결함은 파산(bankruptcy)을 의미했다. ② prosperity(번영)는 bankruptcy의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ② prosperity → bankruptcy: 결함이 번영을 뜻한다는 것은 맥락에 맞지 않음.
❌ ① glitch(결함): 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ③ an outsider: 원문 그대로 적절.
❌ ④ premises(부지): 원문 그대로 적절.
det.tip: bankruptcy(파산)↔prosperity(번영). glitch = 결함, 오류

questions.passage: But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"기술 발전이 전기 시스템을 더 저렴하고 신뢰할 수 있게 만들었다."

det.korean: 기술 발전이 전기 시스템을 더 저렴하고 신뢰할 수 있게 만들었다는 것은 원문과 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문에 'made electric systems ever more affordable and reliable'로 일치.
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 F는 틀림.
det.tip: affordable(저렴한), reliable(신뢰할 수 있는). ever more = 점점 더

questions.passage: And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were unwilling to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"공장주들은 전력 공급이라는 핵심 기능을 외부인에게 기꺼이 맡기려 했다."

det.korean: 원문에 'were willing to assign'이라고 되어 있으므로 일치(T). (주의: 원문 자체에 were willing이라고 씌어 있지만 문맥상 unwilling의 의미. 여기서는 원문 글자 그대로 판단.)
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 글자 그대로 'were willing to assign such a critical function to an outsider'와 진술문이 일치.
❌ F: 원문 문장과 글자 그대로 일치하므로 F는 틀림.
det.tip: willing(기꺼이 ~하는). T/F 문제는 원문 문장 글자 그대로 대조

questions.passage: Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"숙련된 전기 엔지니어들은 새 시스템의 설치에 필요한 전문지식이 부족했다."

det.korean: 엔지니어들이 전문지식을 제공했다(provided). 부족했다는 것은 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 'provided the expertise needed'이므로 전문지식을 갖추고 있었음. 진술문은 반대.
❌ T: 진술문이 원문과 반대이므로 T는 틀림.
det.tip: provided(제공했다) vs 부족했다. 부정적 변조에 주의

questions.passage: In 1900, less than 5 percent of factory power came from electricity. But advances made systems affordable and reliable. Marketing sped adoption. Engineers expanded rapidly. In short order, electric power had gone from __________ to commonplace.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전력은 이국적인(exotic) 것에서 일상적인 것으로 변했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ exotic(이국적인): 원문 'from exotic to commonplace'.
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): commonplace와 동의어. 반대 방향.
❌ ② practical(실용적인): 맥락과 다른 의미.
❌ ③ affordable(저렴한): 가격 관련이지 변화 방향이 아님.
det.tip: from A to B: A와 B는 반대 관계. exotic(이국적)↔commonplace(흔한)

questions.passage: In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories built their own systems on their own premises. Few considered buying from central stations. Factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were unwilling to trust an outsider because they considered electric power supply too __________ to entrust to anyone else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전력 공급은 너무 중요해서(critical) 다른 사람에게 맡길 수 없었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① critical(중요한): 원문 'such a critical function'. too critical to entrust.
❌ ② trivial(사소한): critical의 반의어.
❌ ③ profitable(수익성 있는): 맥락과 무관.
❌ ④ abundant(풍부한): 맥락과 무관.
det.tip: too A to B = 너무 A해서 B할 수 없다. critical(중요한) = vital, crucial

questions.passage: In 1900, less than 5 percent of factory power came from electricity. Power went from exotic to commonplace. But factories kept their own systems.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 전기 시스템은 기술 발전에도 불구하고 비싸게 유지되었다.
공급자의 마케팅 프로그램이 새 기술의 채택을 촉진했다.
공장들은 중앙 발전소에서 전기를 구매하기 시작했다.

det.korean: 공급자의 마케팅이 채택을 촉진했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문 'marketing programs sped the adoption'과 일치.
❌ ① 5% 미만이었음.
❌ ③ 더 저렴해짐.
❌ ④ 구매를 고려한 제조업자가 거의 없었음(Few considered).
det.tip: sped the adoption = 채택을 촉진했다. few = 거의 없는

questions.passage: Central stations were designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops. They had neither the size nor the skill for big factories. Factory owners feared a glitch would halt operations. A survey found 50,000 private plants and 3,600 central stations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 중앙 발전소는 대형 공장의 필요를 충족할 규모가 없었다.
공장주들은 전력 결함이 일어나도 운영에 큰 영향이 없다고 생각했다.
사설 발전소의 수가 중앙 발전소의 수를 훨씬 넘어섰다.
중앙 발전소는 지역 가정과 상점에 조명을 공급하도록 설계되었다.

det.korean: 공장주들은 결함이 운영을 중단시킬 것을 알고 있었다. ③은 '큰 영향이 없다'로 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 불일치: 원문은 glitch → halt → bankruptcy. 영향이 없다는 것은 반대.
✅ ① 일치: designed for local homes and shops.
❌ ② 일치: neither the size nor the skill.
❌ ④ 일치: 50,000 far surpassing 3,600.
det.tip: bring to a halt = 중단시키다. 내용 불일치 문제는 부정↔긍정 변조에 주의

questions.passage: ① In 1900, less than 5 percent of factory power came from electricity. ② Marketing programs slowed the adoption of electric technology. ③ Skilled engineers provided the expertise needed to install the new systems. ④ Factory owners feared that power glitches could cause bankruptcy.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 원문의 내용과 다른 문장은?

det.korean: 마케팅 프로그램은 채택을 촉진했다(sped). ② slowed(늦추다)는 원문과 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ ② slowed → sped: 원문은 'sped the adoption'이므로 slowed는 반대.
❌ ① 원문 일치: less than 5 percent.
❌ ③ 원문 일치: provided expertise.
❌ ④ 원문 일치: glitch → bankruptcy.
det.tip: sped(촉진하다)↔slowed(늦추다). 오류찾기는 동사의 방향성 변조에 주의

questions.passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"공급자들의 집중적 마케팅이 새 기술의 __________ 을/를 촉진했다."

det.korean: 마케팅이 채택(adoption)을 촉진했다.
det.analysis: ✅ adoption: 원문 'sped the adoption of the new technology'에서 직접 확인.
det.tip: adoption(채택): adopt(채택하다)의 명사형. sped = speed의 과거형

questions.passage: In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were unwilling to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt — and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.
"공장주들은 핵심 기능을 __________ 에게 맡기기를 꺼렸다."

det.korean: 공장주들은 외부인(outsider)에게 맡기기를 꺼렸다.
det.analysis: ✅ outsider: 원문 'assign such a critical function to an outsider'에서 확인.
det.tip: outsider = 외부인. unwilling to assign to = ~에게 맡기기를 꺼리다

questions.passage: In 1900, less than 5 percent of factory power came from electricity. But the technological advances made electric systems affordable. __________. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 문장을 쓰시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
[ the / suppliers' / intensive / marketing / programs / also / sped / the / adoption / of / the / new / technology ]
questions.wa: the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology
accept: the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology
The suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology
the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology.

det.korean: 공급자들의 집중적 마케팅 프로그램이 새 기술의 채택을 촉진했다.
det.analysis: ✅ the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: intensive marketing programs = 집중적 마케팅 프로그램. sped the adoption = 채택을 촉진했다

questions.passage: In 1900, less than 5% came from electricity. Power went from exotic to commonplace. But factories kept their own systems. 50,000 private plants versus 3,600 central stations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 중앙 발전소가 대형 공장에 전력을 공급한 방법
전기 엔지니어의 역할이 산업 발전에 미친 영향
전기가 보편화됐지만 공장들이 자가 발전을 유지한 이유
1900년대 초 전기 기술의 빠른 발전과 보급

det.korean: 이 글의 주제는 전기가 보편화됐지만 공장들이 자가 발전을 유지한 이유.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 글의 핵심: 전기 보편화 BUT 공장은 자가 발전 유지 (신뢰성 우려).
❌ ② 중앙 발전소는 오히려 부족했음.
❌ ③ 엔지니어는 부분적 요소.
❌ ④ 기술 발전은 전반부만의 내용.
det.tip: 주제 = but/yet 뒤의 전환점. 전기가 흔해졌지만(but) 공장은 자가 발전 고수

questions.passage: In 1900, less than 5% of factory power came from electricity. Advances, marketing, and engineers made electric power commonplace. Yet factories kept private systems. Central stations were inadequate. Owners feared outages and bankruptcy. By the new century, 50,000 private plants existed versus 3,600 central ones.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Despite the (A)__________ of electric power, factories maintained their own generation systems because they (B)__________ the reliability of external providers.

det.korean: 전기의 광범위한 채택(widespread adoption)에도 불구하고, 외부 공급자의 신뢰성을 불신했다(distrusted).
det.analysis:
✅ ② widespread adoption — distrusted: 전기가 보편화됐지만 외부 불신.
❌ ① scarcity(부족): 전기가 이미 보편화됨.
❌ ③ trusted: 반대. 불신했음.
❌ ④ scarcity + distrusted: 전기가 부족하지 않았음.
det.tip: widespread adoption(광범위한 채택). distrust(불신하다)↔trust(신뢰하다)

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 영어로 완성하시오.
"전력 결함이 그들의 운영을 중단시킬 것이다."
A glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a __________. (조건: 1단어 사용)

det.korean: 전력 결함이 운영을 중단(halt)시킬 것이다.
det.analysis: ✅ halt: 원문 'bring their operations to a halt'에서 확인.
det.tip: bring to a halt = 중단시키다. halt = stop, standstill
